notes.title: Devlog March 2024
notes.content:
It's been two months since the release of the demo. We got tons of feedback from both players and experienced gamedev colleagues. Getting positive feedback is sure nice, but negative or even neutral feedback were the things we tried to focus on since this particular kind of feedback is what makes you understand the weaknesses of your game.

Everyone agreed that Dead Weight was visually stunning. A lot of players said that the game's art style was the reason they decided to give it a try.

When it came to gameplay, opinions were polarized. 

We showcased some of the core game mechanics in the demo: turn-based combat with only ONE action per character and fuel management of the global map. By creating these, we wanted to show that Dead Weight is a hardcore type of game.

On the one hand, it did work; some of the players really appreciated these mechanics. On the other hand, a lot of players have found them too hardcore and borderline unfun. Gamedev professionals said that having only one turn on such small battlefields was too punishing for the players. The fuel management system was also found to be unforgiving and tiresome.

[h2]How to shoot your own leg[/h2]

It became clear that the game mechanics needed some kind of rework. At the same time, we decided that it was finally time to turn Dead Weight into what it was always supposed to be: a roguelike game.

Right when we started working on it, we encountered a huge obstacle. Two months ago, a junior dev who volunteered to work on the game suggested reworking the code part of the game UI. [b]It took us a month to finish.[/b] Can you imagine our faces when we realized that these changes made reworking game mechanics almost impossible?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44799671/3d766465657b89c134b0df4706778e72c6c40a74.png[/img]

It took us one more month to revert all the changes. To be honest, sometimes echos of it can still be seen in the code, and our devs sometimes still wake up in cold sweat with only one word in their heads: "Winhud"...

[h2]The importance of proper documentation[/h2]

As soon as the changes were reverted, we began the long and difficult process of doing reworks. First of all, we wanted to understand what direction we should move in and what changes we wanted to make.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44799671/c463d826923b43e0ba0bd2120b4d40d44f4ee501.jpg[/img]
How it feels to work without a design document

Since the early development stages, we have thought of Dead Wegith as roguelike. That's when we also came up with its unique mechanics. Our first question was: how do we put those inside the boundries of a roguelike genre? We really hoped that an understanding of this would come to us later. It didn't happen. The situation became even worse when it turned out that the core mechanics needed a rework.

All these problems appeared because of one mistake we made. Since we weren't particularly experienced at the beginning of the development, we haven't made a proper design document. We always postponed this important part of the production. That's why we couldn't picture what the final version of our game should look like.

Obviously, we had to make it right. We gathered all the strength that had left after the UI changes and started working on a proper design document. An experienced game designer agreed to help us with it. He has been helping us for two months, and soon the Dead Weight design document will be finished.

[h2]Unclassified documents[/h2]

We've already mentioned that Dead Weight was originally supposed to be a roguelike game. So we reflected this in our design document. 

As in any other roguelike game, the core gameplay of Dead Weight will consist of multiple runs on different maps, akin to the one we had in the demo. Of course, the silimalarity will be mostly visual. In terms of gameplay, things will be different.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44799671/752a15e347a8583cd8c516856b56dec7c5153c98.jpg[/img]
A pirate turned rogue

Each run will happen on a unique map with the main city in the center of it. From this city, the "brunches" of islands will grow. The further an island is from the center, the harder it is to beat it. During a run, the player will have access to 80% of upgrades; the remaining 20% will be available in the hub between runs. Each one of them can be finished either through death or by completing a series of actions that move the story forward.

The player will still be able to move between the islands on their ship, and the fuel management system will still be an important part of gameplay. Although you won't die the moment your ship is out of fuel since the ship also has sails. After the fuel tanks become empty, the player's ship will start to drift. After some time, the player will find themselves near some random (or not) location. This will not only make fuel management less frustrating but also create a completely new gameplay mechanic.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44799671/d3d87d09f6eb7516361459033a3e93b33bcafa65.gif[/img]
POV: your ship started drifting, and you woke up in Skyrim

The most challenging part was the combat system. We had to rework it while keeping it rather unique. We decided to take multiple approaches. During the last two months, we tested four new systems.

Our first idea was to split the action resources into movement points and attack points. It made the game way faster, but also made it harder since the enemies were also using these new rules.

The second idea was simple: keep the combat as it is and just add more characters for the player to control.

The third idea was a mix between our old system and the first one we talked about. In this new system, you could hoard action points and get them by upgrading your character. We really like this variant and most likely will use it. It deepens the gameplay and makes character classes more unique. We also decided to keep the teammates in this variant.

The last idea was inspired by Into the Breach. We tried to let all player characters move at the same time. It highlights the tactical aspect of Dead Weight, but it also makes the game less unique.

[h2]Visual updates[/h2]

While working on balancing and game mechanics, we didn't forget about the visual part of Dead Weight.

We are working on new effects for everything! The battles will look so much cooler now. These effects also made it easier to understand what's going on: it's clear that you got hit with a granade if you see an exlosion, right?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44799671/9d8c11cf019c54a86dbf4cb6acbb06f980e60896.gif[/img]

Besides adding these effects, we also made new falling animations for everyone! No more invisible black holes sucking goblins in. Now everyone will fall into The Abyss while thinking about all the wrong life choices they've made.

[h2]What about marketing?[/h2]

Everything is amazing!

This March, we broke all records. We got more than 12 000 wishlists and got into Top Wishlisted category. All thanks to our Twitter (X) ads campaign we launched two months ago.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44799671/737fa90290aaff5cab319746d85989cd14f49731.png[/img]

Dead Weight got noticed by GamingBible and Turn-Based Lovers. Angory Tom made a whole video about our game with tons of amazing jokes about OSHA violations.

You've probably heard about Princess Hunter and their amazing comics, so the person responsible for these helped us make our own comics. With his assistance, we created four stories and posted them on our social media. People on Reddit loved them! They fell in love with our silly goblin guy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44799671/e94c78407b7abbeecc47adf59cb89a83d9153b31.jpg[/img]
The man of your dreams

Our team became bigger! Recently, we hired one more really nice developer. Now six people are working on Dead Weight.

We have even more cool stuff planned. We want to make sure that everyone and their mother know about Dead Weight! 
Apparently, now we have fans all over the world, so we are working on a new demo version, and we will make sure to add more supported languages and make it as accessible as possible.

[h2]March (and February) in numbers[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44799671/259e2c62097bd55c90ba7776433c60490077b28d.png[/img]
He-he, LEET

[list]
[*] 6 devs shocked by the number of wishlists
[*] 100+ hours spent on reverting the UI changes
[*] 1 [strike]almost[/strike] finished design document
[*] 420 cups of tea were drunk by devs
[*] 4 variants of the combat system were done
[*] gained more than 1 300 position in Top wishlisted
[*] got more than 12 000 wishlists
[*] 5 articles about Dead Weight were released in the media
[*] 1 new version of the demo is in the works
[/list]

notes.title: Devlog January 2024
notes.content:
A few months ago, we decided to release our demo in January. Well, [b]we effed it up[/b], and we will tell you how it happened.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44799671/229b0bae7c2a9e810fb94672037e1383351ea7a0.png[/img]

Dead Weight IS pirates, and pirates ARE Dead Weight. That's why we couldn't miss Pirates vs. Ninjas Steam Fest. We decided to participate in it with a demo version of our game.

Our team had been the creating demo since the end of November. Back then, we decided to turn all the gameplay sketches we created into an hour-long gaming experience. To do so, we had to stop developing new game mechanincs and focus on polishing the already existing ones. We even asked one of our testers to record a playthrough, which we broadcasted on our Steam page.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44799671/9f6384c43e59db6f19f915dc762bc8af34a0603a.png[/img]Yo-ho-ho and a bottle of sake.

The application has been sent and approved, and the demo is almost ready, so what could go wrong, right? Right? We forgot to submit our demo for Steam moderation...

The festival is about to start, and our demo still hasn't been approved yet. We started to try to come up with a way out. Some of our colleagues told us the approval process might take up to two weeks. We got scared and even made a damage control post about how sorry we are that we have to postpone the release.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44799671/0d6acb4b680d397dfafdb08f8d0cd404ce976051.png[/img]

Soon, it dawned on us that we had already requested a few Steam keys to test our demo. So, why shouldn't we request even more keys, which we can give to everyone who's willing to play Dead Weight?

Immediately, we requested 1000 (!) keys and got them all [b]ONE[/b] hour before the start of the festival. Here we faced one more challenge. How can we possibly give these keys to hundreds of people without spending hours doing it? Well, we found a way. With only a few energy drink cans, a dozen Youtube turotials, and a couple of calls, we made a chatbot that we used to give the keys to the players.

Thanks to this bot, 250 people got their keys in a week. After that, we got lucky again, and our demo finally got approved after only 5 days instead of two weeks, and we were able to release it with open access.

We got another quest. We were getting dozens of feedback messages from our players, which had to be analyzed. We had to do it manually... Every day started and ended with replying to the feedback we got. Players were willing not only to share their impression of the game but also to share all the bugs they found. We had no idea that some of them could even exist.

We are grateful for pointing out all the things we missed. Of course, we have a few dozen testers doing it for us, but having hundreds of new players each with a unique point of view helps us a lot.

Some players encountered optimisation issues. They reported that Dead Weight was using, surprisingly, a lot of VRAM. We strive to make our game as accessible as possible, that's why this issue has the highest priority for us.

[h1]The results of the festival[/h1]

The festival ended on January 29th. Here are some results we got: 250 activated keys, 800 wishlists. 600 people played our demo, with a median playtime of 25 minutes. Some of them even spent up to 6 hours playing Dead Weight. Sounds cool, right?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44799671/1e5287fca7523fc4451030abb8ba10dc627a924b.png[/img]

Not really... Out of all 800 wishlists, only 80 were from non-Russian-speaking countries. We do love our Russian-speaking fans, but for a game to be successful it definitely needs to have English-speaking fans as well... It means that the festival didn't fulfill its goal of attracting foreign audience.

[h1]What's next?[/h1]

Despite all the  difficulties we faced and the unsatisfactory results of the festival, we aren't ready to give up. We are motivated by [b]YOU[/b] and all the positive feedback you keep giving us! That's why we will continue to make and improve Dead Weight.

We decided not to delist the demo after the end of the festival since a lot of stuff went sideways for us and we couldn't achieve everything we planned. Some of you were saying that there isn't enough variability in the gameplay of our demo, so we are working on fixing it by adding a new enemy faction of pirate mercenaries.

Those who played the first ever version of Dead Weight on itch.io might recognise these fellas. Since when, we have had a new artist and wanted to change their design to match the rest of the characters. Now you'll have to fight not only goblins but also these experienced sky wolves too. It’s not gonna be easy!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44799671/6ee260f6734b41e9d1792074a74547a92474a7e0.png[/img]Ready for battle!

Apart from the new faction, we are working on improving game visuals by adding various VFX. We are also looking for new ways to improve the core gameplay.

Moreover, we plan to add new playable characters to the game. Some of you might have seen their early concepts on our social media. We'll tell you a secret: we redesigned them. Try to guess what they look like now. Here is a small tip:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44799671/f73c60cae5de75a10004e79cb6624e2ee1e5948c.jpg[/img]Can you guess the new characters' designs?

January in numbers
[list]
[*] 1 released demo
[*] 6 developers are tired
[*] 600 people played the demo
[*] 43 bugs were fixed
[*] got 2125 wishlists 
[*] drunk 76 cups of coffee
[*] listened to lofi hip hop radio - beats to relax/study to for 103 hours
[*] analyzed 147 feedback messages
[*] 1 new faction is about to be added
[/list]

notes.title: Devlog December 2023
notes.content:
This December was rich with events for our small team. We implemented a new playtest system, and after that, our testers sent us tons of feedback. When we finished analyzing it, we decided to make some changes to our new battle UI and the previolsy made tutorial. Oh, and our Steam page is finally online!

[h2]Steam and marketing[/h2]

Our small dream has finally been fulfilled: Dead Weight is finally on Steam, surrounded by our beloved games. The game release might still be far, but this thought alone warms our gaming-loving hearts... You can warm them too by adding Dead Weight to your wishlist!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44799671/548736c511ded88c032e0d3b5ff6c2454806be95.png[/img]

Wanna get some inside marketing info? Of course you do! In 6 days we got more than 600 wishlists. UTM links only tracked 1/3 of them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44799671/3e6f47b3ff7caa131bbd275e62130f6103412490.png[/img]

Most of our wishlists came from Russia, thanks to our social media pages. The US got second place mainly because our first Reddit post ever got a lot of attention.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44799671/dcec16c13a408d5284e2014e899fd88cdbf827bf.png[/img]

[h2]Live playtests and feedback[/h2]

During our previous playtests, we learned that most of the players found our game too complicated. To solve this issue, we decided to change our battle UI and create a complete tutorial section. After it was all done we needed someone to test it. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44799671/922548c82a2e8d1ecb4810e91e170b9ac89275f4.png[/img][i]Dead Weight game designer watching the livetesting.[/i]

That's why we decided to try live testing for the first time. A few people who were willing to participate and had never played Dead Weight before were selected. Later, we called them on Discord and asked them to play the new tutorial section on stream. 

Every player had the exact same set of tasks, but they all found different ways to solve them. Some of them were unquestioningly following all the tips from the mysterious voice inside their heads. Others decided to go their own way.

We noticed four different types of players:
[olist]
[*]The player reads and follows all the tips we left them. For this type of player, completing the tutorial sections was pretty easy.
[*]The player still reads the tips but misses a lot of important information. It leads to misunderstanding of some core game mechanincs. For this type of player, completing the tutorial section was difficult, but still doable.
[*]The player decides not to read the tips and hopes to use their gaming experience to solve the tasks. Because of that, they struggle with completing the tasks and get negative experience with the game.
[*]The player reads the tips but does not want to follow them. Instead, they want to stress-test the game. They do all they can to find bugs and exploits. Such a playthrough takes a lot of time, but it's so interesting to watch.
[/olist]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44799671/7768197ff41ded7c29b18f47df3051662481f90d.png[/img][i]500 fuel units? Something isn't right here.[/i]

After the first couple of tests, we made some adjustments based on the testers' feedback. We made the tips shorter and highlighted key words to make them easier to understand, added some restrictions to traveling to stop players from getting lost, fixed a few bugs, and created save points.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44799671/15592af6ce3b574f68090e8eaddf4510fb0d176f.png[/img]
[i]The voice in your head can be pretty useful.[/i]

At first, we hoped that the players would finish the tutorial in 30-40 minutes. In reality, they only managed to complete roughly 40% of it in that time. That's why we decided to force an ending at 40% of the tutorial. Although there is still a way to bypass the ending and see the remaining 60%. Maybe someone will find a way to do it...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44799671/c7513035723cd1252b6c71e3347e01a2d9e1b2d6.png[/img]
[h2]UI[/h2]

We wrote a lot about UI changes in our previous devlogs, but, sadly, they aren't (yet?) translated. The moment we received some feedback regarding these changes, we decided to make some changes to it. 

During live tests, it became obvious how hard it was for the player to notice that the enemy was preparing an attack. To fix it, we replaced the old attack indicator with a new one. Some of you will definetly find it familiar...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44799671/92ff6e622a938271867c0a52184d65dd6d32e694.jpg[/img]
[i]Moments before disaster.[/i]

This is still a temporary solution. We are thinking about whether we should add a special attack preparation animation or not.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44799671/b0b5c4fda9e77ce4d2936a30efdb5ea5b28fa038.png[/img]
[i]RIP[/i]

[h2]In December we:[/h2]
[list]
[*] made 172 build updates
[*] got 666 wishlists
[*] got 2 followers who wanted to make a donation
[*] got 19 000 impressions on Reddit
[*] [b]planned 1 demo release on Q1 2024[/b]
[*] got 2 sick team members
[*] ate 78 tangerines
[*] spent 10+ hours on live testing 
[*] drank 722 cups of tea
[*] organized 1 party
[*] got 21 700 impressions on Steam
[*] prepared 5 holiday animations for our social media pages 
[/list]

[h2] Thank you for the support! See you in the next year <3 [/h2]
